always easy enough to get an appointment, my GP was usually well-natured and I was understanding when it came to delays and when staff were in a bad mood (the NHS overworks its staff), but in my experience this practice is completely negligent when it comes to treating someone with a mental illness.

During a bad episode and upon losing 10kg because of it the response was 'well the sun is shining outside so hopefully that will make this go away' and 'just try eating lots of high-calorie foods like cakes and biscuits' - absolutely shocking considering the state I was in and how low my BMI was. I made an appointment with a different GP in the same practice who said I was 'probably just stressed' given my life circumstances at the time and made no attempt to even give advice, so I didn't see her again.

I was prescribed medication on another occasion by my GP and she laughed when she discovered that not only did I have most of the common and uncommon side effects but some of the rare ones too. It wasn't funny! They were making my life quite difficult and I knew something wasn't right but was told to persist, when I eventually changed GP practices I was immediately switched medications because the one I was on had caused me to develop another condition which would have been potentially life-threatening if it got any worse. Believe it or not, I had said that I was worried I had developed this condition to the GP in Apsley Street when discussing my side effects 6 months earlier! She had looked up the condition in one of her books, shrugged and said she hadn't heard of it, and then my worries were discarded.

It's hard having to monitor your condition and assess the efficacy of the medication when you're unable to think straight. I knew I was becoming more and more unwell but I'm not the doctor, so I put my trust in this GP to help me get better. I've never heard of such irresponsible 'care' from a medical professional before, seemingly no knowledge of mental illnesses or their progression and set me back over a year in my recovery.

Oh, and I was bruised every time I got blood taken from either the nurse or my GP, and one time when my GP did it she accidentally went straight through my vein into a ligament! She was honest about it at least, but then said it was because I was 'too skinny', as she is used to 'larger patients'.
